s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of loss of consciousness with neck and back pain, associated with abnormal cardiac rhythms and family history of sudden cardiac death
salient_findings: Episode of neck and back pain and loss of consciousness
Family history of sudden cardiac death at a young age
key_facts: Patient is a 47-year-old woman
Patient has controllable hypertension
Patient experienced an episode of neck and back pain and loss of consciousness
Patient had a similar episode one year prior
Family history of sudden cardiac death at a young age
Patient's uncle and two sisters had sudden cardiac death
Patient took calcium channel blocker for about one month after first episode
Body temperature: 37.5°C
Heart rate: 68 bpm
Blood pressure: 145/50 mmHg
Pupils: equal at 3.5 mm with sluggish light reflex
Absent corneal reflex
Normal lung auscultation
Mild hyperglycemia (11.92 mmol/L)
Elevated transaminases (ALT 146 U/L, AST 89 U/L)
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.213, PCO2 35.8 mmHg, PO2 396.1 mmHg, HCO3− 14.1 mmol/L, O2 saturation 99.7%, lactate 11.53 mmol/L
Initial troponin I, D-dimer, and BNP levels were normal
Head and chest CT scans were unremarkable
Coronary angiography revealed normal left and right coronary arteries
Left ventricular ejection fraction: 59%
ECG showed complete atrioventricular block with inferior ST-segment elevation (heart rate 45 bpm) during first episode
ECG showed junctional escape rhythm (heart rate 32 bpm) during second episode
Whole exome sequencing performed on patient and family members showed no abnormalities

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of sudden cardiac death and abnormal cardiac rhythms

shortlist.label: Brugada syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal cardiac rhythms and family history of sudden cardiac death

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of sudden cardiac death and abnormal cardiac rhythms

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of loss of consciousness with abnormal cardiac rhythms and family history of sudden cardiac death

raw.rationale: The patient's family history of sudden cardiac death at a young age, combined with her own episodes of loss of consciousness and abnormal ECG findings, including complete atrioventricular block and junctional escape rhythm, suggest a diagnosis of Long QT syndrome. The normal coronary angiography and left ventricular ejection fraction also support this diagnosis, as Long QT syndrome is a primary electrical disorder rather than a structural heart disease.

rejected.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: While this condition can cause loss of consciousness and abnormal ECG findings, the patient's family history and ECG results are more suggestive of Long QT syndrome.

rejected.label: Brugada syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's ECG findings do not show the characteristic ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3 that is typical of Brugada syndrome.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's normal left ventricular ejection fraction and lack of symptoms suggestive of obstructive cardiomyopathy make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's normal coronary angiography and left ventricular ejection fraction, combined with the lack of symptoms suggestive of right ventricular dysfunction, make this diagnosis less likely.
